message:
docs(policy): the swap failure note was wrong, and two rules fought each other

I wrote that a failed swap leaves the previous release published because the .tmp
files get removed. That is not what the script does. The two renames are chained with
&& (gnlink_deploy.sh:440), so if the first succeeds and the second does not, the
manifest is new and the signature is old, and removing the .tmp files does not undo
it. The script's own die message says the previous release is still published, and it
is wrong for that case -- I used this code as the authority for the atomicity
correction and then inherited its optimistic failure message without checking it. A
partial swap has no guaranteed rollback: restore the exact backup pair by hand and
report the publish as a blocker. The message at :442 joins :445 on the follow-up list;
neither is touched here, as this is docs-only.

Pinning the tested binary to the release candidate hash contradicted the clause two
sections earlier that allows an asInvoker, test-signed build. Split: a shipping
candidate is pinned exactly, while a product-equivalent test build is pinned by source
commit, shared UI asset hashes, a stated build delta and a per-artifact mapping -- the
executables may differ, and what that build cannot prove is written beside it.

"Task completion runs to the behaviour check" plus "unverified stays working" meant a
single UAC prompt could hold a task open forever and the final report never came --
which happened today. When everything not requiring elevation is verified, deployed
and checked from outside, that can be reported as agent work complete, user field test
pending, with success left explicitly unconfirmed. An unimplemented button, or a
required behaviour that could have been verified automatically and was not, still
blocks completion.

Also scoped two overstatements: the 32Hz and 0x80070005 figures are measurements from
this machine rather than a property of RDP, and "the Client can be driven" holds
within the same privilege session and the tools actually demonstrated -- a physical
mouse click inside the WebView is not among them.
